name: GEER TYPE AGING OVEN
desc: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS INNO-XAGO-V-220 Geer Type Aging Oven is a specialized thermal testing chamber designed strictly to evaluate the degradation and aging characteristics of plastics, rubber, and polymer samples in accordance with ISO, JIS, and ASTM international standards.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS GEER TYPE AGING OVEN is a precision thermal testing chamber engineered to simulate accelerated aging conditions for plastics, rubber, and polymer materials in strict accordance with ISO, JIS, and ASTM international standards. This oven employs a forced-air convection system with adjustable air exchange rates (5 to 300 times per hour at 80°C) to replicate oxidative and thermal degradation environments. The rotating double-layered specimen rack (8–10 rpm) ensures uniform exposure of test specimens to heat and airflow, preventing localized temperature gradients. Doctors, B.Sc/M.Sc students, PhD researchers, and chemists utilize this oven to evaluate long-term stability, oxidation resistance, tensile strength retention, and color fastness of materials such as polyethylene, polypropylene, PVC, natural rubber, and silicone elastomers. The PID controller maintains temperature accuracy of ±0.5°C up to 300°C, enabling precise simulation of service conditions for automotive components, cable insulation, and medical-grade polymers. The stainless steel 304 chamber with high-density rock wool insulation minimizes heat loss, while the toughened glass observation window and internal illumination allow real-time monitoring without disturbing the thermal equilibrium. This instrument is essential for quality control, material certification, and research on degradation kinetics, including the measurement of volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions and antioxidant depletion in polymer matrices.
sop: Ensure the oven is placed on a stable, level surface and lock the caster wheel brakes to prevent movement.
Connect the power supply to a 220V, 50Hz grounded electrical outlet and verify the fuse safety switch is in the OFF position before startup.
Open the insulated solid door using the sturdy handle and load test specimens onto the rotating double-layered specimen rack, ensuring balanced distribution to avoid vibration.
Close the door securely, confirming the high-temperature silicone rubber gasket forms a tight seal.
Turn ON the main power switch and switch ON the inner chamber illumination light if visual monitoring is required.
Press the 'SET' button once on the PID temperature controller.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target temperature (e.g., 100°C for standard ISO 188 aging of rubber).
Press 'SET' again to lock the target temperature value into the controller memory.
Set the in-built timer for the desired dwell time (e.g., 72 hours for long-term aging) by pressing the timer SET button and using arrow keys.
Adjust the ventilation damper to achieve the required air exchange rate (e.g., 50 times per hour at 80°C) as per the test standard.
Start the rotation mechanism by pressing the rotation ON switch; verify the specimen rack rotates at 8–10 rpm.
Monitor the temperature display and rotation status periodically through the toughened glass window; do not open the door during high-temperature operation.
After the test duration is complete, switch OFF the heater and rotation, but allow the oven to cool naturally to below 50°C before opening the door.
Turn OFF the main power switch, open the door cautiously, and remove specimens using heat-resistant gloves and tongs.

SAFETY WARNING: Never open the oven door while the chamber temperature exceeds 50°C, as sudden cool air ingress can cause thermal shock to specimens and risk burns; always wear heat-resistant gloves, safety goggles, and a lab coat, and ensure the room is well-ventilated to avoid inhalation of any volatile degradation byproducts.
